spec.Definition:
Content with a genuinely non-specific subject — a
reaction, mood, or relatable moment with no recoverable topic beyond
"this resonated," even after the full evidence hierarchy is applied.
spec.Include when:
caption/hashtags/OCR/account signal collectively fail to
support any of the other 37 categories, *and* the failure isn't due to a
known extraction defect.
spec.Exclude when:
any specific, nameable subject is present (a product, a
place, a person, a skill, an event) — even briefly or thinly stated.
spec.Primary evidence:
absence of positive evidence elsewhere, not evidence
for General itself — General is never selected by a positive signal, only
by exhaustion of the other 37.
spec.Positive signals:
none — this category has no positive signal set by
design. Treat any rule that tries to give General a positive trigger as a
bug.
spec.Negative signals:
any hashtag naming a real entity (person, place,
brand, skill); any caption sentence with a concrete noun beyond a
feeling-word.
spec.Confusable categories:
Uncategorized / No Content Available (the
critical distinction — see Section 5); every other category is
"confusable" in the sense that General is the default loser against all
of them.
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
General never wins a tie. If any other
category clears even a thin evidentiary bar, that category wins.
spec.Language handling:
no special handling — a Tamil/Tanglish caption with
no recoverable topic is General exactly as an English one would be; the
absence-of-topic test is language-independent.
spec.Format vs. subject rule:
neither — General is explicitly an
evidence-state, not a format or a subject. It should be thought of as "no
subject identified," structurally different from "video content."
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
none required to *assign* General — it
requires the *absence* of evidence for anything else, which is a
different kind of check (exhaustion, not accumulation).
spec.General fallback interaction: N/A — this is the fallback.
spec.Review trigger:
any General assignment on a caption that also matches
the known metadata-only-caption extraction pattern (Section 5) must
carry `needs_review: true`, not be treated as a confident General.
spec.Positive examples:
**none confirmed in the evidence base.** Across all
60 Sorti-touched Reels investigated in this project, zero produced a
positive, independently-confirmed "this is genuinely General" result —
every General-origin item checked so far turned out to have a recoverable
topic. This is stated plainly rather than inventing an example; it means
General's correctness has not yet been positively demonstrated, only its
current over-use has been demonstrated repeatedly.

spec.Definition:
The evidence itself is unavailable or unusable — not a
topic judgment at all, a statement about data quality.
spec.Include when:
caption field is empty, is the literal placeholder
`"(No caption text available for this Reel.)"`, or matches the confirmed
metadata-only-caption pattern (`"97K likes, 127 comments - username on
date"`) with no other usable field (title, OCR) providing content.
spec.Exclude when:
any real words exist in the caption, even thin or
generic ones ("Just for fun keep smiling 😊" is General, not
Uncategorized — it has real, if generic, text).
spec.Primary evidence: the caption field's literal content/absence.
spec.Positive signals:
empty string; the literal no-caption placeholder;
the regex-confirmed engagement-metadata pattern.
spec.Negative signals: any actual sentence, even a short or generic one.
spec.Confusable categories:
General (see Section 5 for the precise
operational test separating the two).
spec.Language handling:
N/A — the test is about presence/absence of text,
not its language.
spec.Format vs. subject rule:
neither — same evidence-state nature as
General, one level more extreme (no evidence at all vs. evidence that
doesn't resolve to a topic).
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
zero, by definition — this is the
"below minimum evidence" category.
spec.General fallback interaction:
Uncategorized is checked *before*
General in the evidence hierarchy — if the caption is truly empty,
Uncategorized applies directly; General is only reached once there's
*something* to have failed to resolve.
spec.Review trigger:
any Uncategorized assignment on a caption matching the
metadata-only pattern specifically (not a truly empty caption) should
carry `needs_review: true`, since that pattern is the one under active
suspicion of being an extraction bug rather than genuinely absent content
(Section 5, Caption Extraction Audit from the prior benchmark spec).
spec.Positive examples:
`DF5I4VBMZD1`, `DNzjg6RZhce`, `DL2c1LWCoT8` — all
three carry the literal `"(No caption text available for this Reel.)"`
placeholder, confirmed from the earlier semantic-model benchmark work.

spec.Definition:
General-purpose programming education, coding concepts,
and language tutorials not specific to web front-ends, deployment/infra,
or data/analytics work, and not specifically interview/DSA-prep framed.
spec.Include when:
content teaches or discusses programming languages,
syntax, or concepts (any language) without a web-, infra-, data-, or
interview-specific frame.
spec.Exclude when:
the web/infra/data/interview-specific frame is present
(routes to the sibling category instead).
spec.Primary evidence:
caption/hashtags naming a programming language or
concept directly.
spec.Positive signals:
language names (Java, Python, C++) without a
qualifying domain word; "learn to code," "programming concepts," coding
memes.
spec.Negative signals:
"interview," "DSA," "placement" (→ Java/Programming
Interview Prep); "website," "frontend," "React" (→ Web Development);
"deploy," "pipeline," "Docker" (→ DevOps); "SQL," "data analyst" (→ Data
Science); consumer-audience framing with no code shown (→ Technology /
Gadgets).
spec.Confusable categories:
Java / Programming Interview Prep, Web
Development, DevOps / Software Engineering, Data Science / Analytics,
Technology / Gadgets.
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
see Section 4 boundary matrix — resolved
by domain-specific keyword presence, not by "Programming" being a
catch-all default for anything code-adjacent.
spec.Language handling:
Tanglish coding content (e.g., Tamil words used as
variable-name jokes in an otherwise-genuine Python tutorial) still counts
as Programming if the actual instructional content is programming — the
language of the surrounding commentary doesn't change the subject.
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
at least one specific language/concept
name, not just the word "coding" or "tech" alone.
spec.General fallback interaction:
a caption that only says "coding is
hard lol" with no specific language/concept named and no code shown is
NOT enough for this category — check Comedy & Entertainment (General)
first (the "Engineering-means-comedy" pattern applies here too), then
General.
spec.Review trigger:
caption contains a language name AND explicit
comedic/meme framing with no real instructional content (ambiguous
between this category and Comedy) — flag for review rather than guessing.
spec.Positive examples:
`DSDEAMNAYIA` ("Why Java is faster than python"),
`Dcvwx2qNp9k` ("45-Day DSA with Python Batch 1... coding interviews" —
note this one actually leans toward Java/Programming Interview Prep given
the explicit interview framing, illustrating the boundary in practice),
`Cr-ClVFpfyB` (Python code example using Tamil-comedy variable names,
still genuinely teaching syntax).

spec.Definition:
Coding-interview and DSA-preparation content, specific to
landing a technical job — language-agnostic in principle but named "Java"
because that's the dominant language observed in this library's interview
content.
spec.Include when:
content is explicitly interview/placement/DSA-prep
framed, regardless of which language is used.
spec.Exclude when:
general language teaching with no interview/placement
framing (→ Programming / Coding General).
spec.Primary evidence:
explicit interview/DSA/placement language in
caption or hashtags.
spec.Positive signals:
"interview questions," "DSA," "placement,"
"coding round," "45-day challenge... interviews."
spec.Negative signals:
no interview/placement framing at all — a Java
tutorial with no interview angle is Programming / Coding General, not
this category, regardless of language.
spec.Confusable categories:
Programming / Coding General, Career / Jobs &
Hiring (interview *content* vs. interview *logistics/opportunities*),
Resume & Interview Preparation (technical coding interviews specifically
vs. general interview conduct/resume content).
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
if the content is a technical
coding/DSA question itself → this category. If it's about interview
*etiquette*, *scheduling*, or *resume-building* with no actual coding
content → Resume & Interview Preparation. If it's about *finding* the
interview opportunity → Career / Jobs & Hiring.
spec.Language handling:
Tanglish interview-prep content (confirmed real,
`DVODEUaEtM-`) is fully in-scope — language of narration doesn't change
subject.
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
explicit interview/DSA/placement
language, not just the presence of code.
spec.General fallback interaction:
rare — interview-prep content almost
always has enough specific signal to avoid General.
spec.Review trigger:
content that mixes genuine DSA teaching with heavy
comedic framing (rare but possible) — flag rather than force a choice.
spec.Positive examples:
`DbQsKoBzRQt` ("Java 50 interview questions"),
`DH2fIFgzVsG` ("Java is tough until..."), `DVODEUaEtM-` (Sorti-confirmed
"Software Engineering" — Tanglish, Zoho-specific coding-interview
content, DSA-roadmap framing).

spec.Definition:
Building, styling, or deploying websites/web
applications — frontend, backend-for-web, or web-specific tooling and
business (pricing, client work).
spec.Include when:
content is about a website/web-app as the deliverable
— design, code, or the business of building one.
spec.Exclude when:
the content is general backend/infra with no web-page
framing (→ DevOps), or general programming with no web subject (→
Programming / Coding General).
spec.Primary evidence:
caption/hashtags naming web-specific terms (React,
frontend, website, UI/UX-for-web, web design pricing).
spec.Positive signals:
`#webdevelopment`, `#website`, `#react`, `#frontend`,
`#webdesign`, client/pricing language tied explicitly to a website
deliverable.
spec.Negative signals:
generic "portfolio"/"developer" language with no
web-specific term; deployment/infra language with no page/site framing
(→ DevOps).
spec.Confusable categories:
Programming / Coding General, DevOps / Software
Engineering, Art & Creativity (web *design* specifically, aesthetic
framing).
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
is a website/web-app the explicit
deliverable? → Web Development. Is the deliverable a static visual design
with no code/site implied? → Art & Creativity. Is the focus
infrastructure/deployment with no page-level framing? → DevOps.
spec.Language handling:
no special handling needed — web-dev terminology
is consistently English/technical regardless of surrounding
Tamil/Tanglish commentary.
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
at least one web-specific term, not just
"developer" or "tech" alone (those alone → Programming / Coding General
or Technology / Gadgets depending on audience).
spec.General fallback interaction:
the confirmed historical failure case
(`DdGQC_tRDCw`, `DQ3eXFDkQ2X`) — a dismissive/generic opening line drowning
out a decisive `#webdesign` signal, both incorrectly reached General
under the legacy classifier. Do not let opening-line tone override a
clear web-specific hashtag later in the caption.
spec.Review trigger:
caption has web-specific tags but the described
deliverable is ambiguous between a website and a broader digital product
— flag rather than guess.
spec.Positive examples:
`DNQvckKo7VB` ("How DNS Works in 60 Seconds"),
`DdGQC_tRDCw` (Sorti-confirmed "Web Design," website pricing guide),
`DQ3eXFDkQ2X` (Sorti-confirmed "Engineering" per Sorti's own inconsistent
label, but description confirms web-dev/React/portfolio content).

Using, reviewing, or explaining AI products (ChatGPT,
Claude, Gemini, image/video generators) as tools — not the underlying
engineering of building them.
spec.Include when:
content names or demos a specific AI product/tool/
feature.
spec.Exclude when:
content uses AI/product names as decoration on
otherwise-unrelated content (e.g., a personal-anecdote video with an
incidental `#chatgpt` tag and no actual AI content — confirmed real
failure case, `DRVQX4RAafH`, correctly excluded to General); or when
"AI" appears only as generic aspirational language with no product named
(→ Motivation & Self Improvement, per the coconut-water-case exclusion
rule).
spec.Primary evidence:
a named AI product or a demonstrated AI-tool
feature/output.
spec.Positive signals:
"ChatGPT," "Claude," "Gemini," specific AI-tool
feature names, AI-generated content shown as the subject.
spec.Negative signals:
AI-adjacent hashtag with no actual AI content
visible in caption/description; generic "AI will change everything"
language with no product named.
spec.Confusable categories:
Motivation & Self Improvement (the confirmed
false-attractor pattern — aspirational language wrapping a specific
product should route here, not there, but generic aspirational language
about AI-as-a-trend with no product belongs in Motivation instead),
Data Science / Analytics (AI-as-consumer-tool vs. AI/ML-as-engineering-
discipline — this category is for the former).
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
is a specific product/feature named and
demonstrated? → AI Tools. Is the language generic/aspirational with no
product? → Motivation & Self Improvement.
spec.Language handling: no special handling needed.
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
a named AI product, not just the letters
"AI" in a hashtag.
spec.General fallback interaction:
an AI-hashtagged caption with zero real
AI content and zero other topic (like `DRVQX4RAafH`) correctly goes to
General, not here — the hashtag is not sufficient evidence alone.
spec.Review trigger:
caption names an AI product but the actual
demonstrated content is ambiguous or the hashtag looks tacked-on — flag.
spec.Positive examples:
`DbIawIYsj19` ("ChatGPT Pro worth Rs. 10,699 for
free"), `DZ31KYDRoMk` ("four techniques to reduce the llm api cost"),
`DPn0DPBDCiB` (Sorti-confirmed "Guides," AI video character-swap tool,

spec.Definition:
Finding, changing, or getting hired for a job — the
search/discovery/opportunity side, not performance once hired.
spec.Include when:
content is about job openings, hiring drives, career-
change strategy, or career-path roadmaps.
spec.Exclude when:
content is about on-the-job growth/culture (→ Career
Growth & Workplace) or resume/interview-performance specifics (→ Resume &
Interview Preparation).
spec.Primary evidence:
caption naming job openings, hiring, or career-path
language.
spec.Positive signals:
"jobs," "hiring," "internship," "placement,"
"vacancy," "get hired."
spec.Negative signals:
on-the-job culture/advice language with no
search/discovery framing.
spec.Confusable categories:
Career Growth & Workplace, Resume & Interview
Preparation, AI Tools & Generative AI (when "get hired" outcome-framing
wraps a tech/AI subject).
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
is the content about *finding/landing*
an opportunity? → Career / Jobs & Hiring. Is it about *performing well*
once you have an interview lined up? → Resume & Interview Preparation.
Is it about life *after* being hired? → Career Growth & Workplace. Does

spec.Minimum evidence requirement: explicit job-search/hiring language.
spec.General fallback interaction:
uncommon — job-search content tends to
carry clear signal.
spec.Review trigger:
content genuinely ambiguous between this and Career
Growth & Workplace (e.g., "how I changed careers" could be either) — flag
if the search-vs-growth framing isn't clear.
spec.Positive examples:
`Dcga0EbyQht` ("VLSI Design Internship Alert"),
`DW6TaklveYy` ("placement preparation roadmap"), `DQeNW_cDNdF`
(Sorti-confirmed "Guides," AI/tech projects framed around "get hired").

spec.Definition:
On-the-job advice — promotions, workplace culture, soft
skills, professional communication — once already employed.
spec.Include when:
content is substantive workplace/career advice with no
comedic/meme framing.
spec.Exclude when:
the content is explicitly comedy/meme-framed, even if
set in an office (→ Comedy & Entertainment (General), see Rule A below);
or is about finding a job rather than growing in one (→ Career / Jobs &
Hiring).
spec.Primary evidence: substantive advice content, no joke/meme framing.
spec.Positive signals:
"salary negotiation," "promotion," "workplace
culture," "professional communication," concrete actionable claims.
spec.Negative signals:
explicit "meme," "relatable," "funny," "tag your
colleague" framing with no actual advice content — this is the single
most important negative signal for this category (see Rule A).
spec.Confusable categories:
Comedy & Entertainment (General) (the
confirmed dominant confusion pattern — 5 instances across this project's
evidence base), Career / Jobs & Hiring.
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
**Rule A, formalized**: if the
description or caption explicitly frames the content as comedy/meme/joke
(the words "comedy," "meme," "funny," "relatable," or a "tag someone"
call-to-action with no actual advice), Comedy & Entertainment (General)
wins regardless of the office/work subject matter. If the content gives
genuine, actionable workplace/HR/professional-communication guidance with
no joke framing, this category wins. Concrete boundary examples:
`DZIV16bNCH_` (Sorti: "relatable work escalation meme") → Comedy, not this
category, despite being entirely about office life. `DNx1xKIZmap`
(Sorti-confirmed, actual OOO-email-writing technique) → this category,
because it's genuine advice, not a joke.
spec.Language handling: no special handling needed.
spec.Format vs. subject rule:
subject, but requires a format check
(non-comedic) as a gate — see Rule A.
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
at least one concrete, actionable
workplace claim, not just an office setting.
spec.General fallback interaction:
the confirmed historical failure case —
multiple Sorti-validated examples (`DP09KRskgPj`, `DNx1xKIZmap`,
`DauYntJjqTX`) were dumped to General despite substantive workplace
content.
spec.Review trigger:
content where the comedy-vs-advice framing is
genuinely unclear — flag rather than guess.
spec.Positive examples:
`Dci6N3Ihs9T` ("5 things you're saying wrong on
your offer call"), `DWwdG4dCToL` (EOD update email format),
`DNx1xKIZmap` (Sorti-confirmed "Communication," OOO email tip),
`DP09KRskgPj` (Sorti-confirmed "Employee Rights," Supreme Court
workplace-accident ruling — imperfect fit, documented taxonomy gap,
routed here as best-available).

spec.Definition:

framed comedic/meme content — not triggered by a Tamil-adjacent account
name or hashtag alone.

or a single hashtag) contains Tamil script, genuine Tanglish, or explicit
Tamil-cultural-comedic framing (named Tamil comedians, Tamil meme-format

**Rule I, formalized**: the only Tamil signal is the
account name being Tamil-sounding, or a single generic `#tamil` hashtag
with no Tamil content in the caption body itself (→ Comedy & Entertainment
(General) instead).
spec.Primary evidence:
genuine Tamil-script/Tanglish text in the caption,
or an explicit Tamil-comedic-culture reference (a named Tamil comedian, a
recognized Tamil meme template).
spec.Negative signals:
Tamil-sounding account name with English-only
caption and no Tamil-cultural comedic reference; a single generic
`#tamil` hashtag with otherwise language-agnostic joke content.
spec.Confusable categories:
Comedy & Entertainment (General) (Rule I),
Kollywood / Tamil Movie Fan Edits (the joke-vs-tribute distinction,
carried over unchanged from the original taxonomy proposal: fan
tribute/nostalgia → Kollywood; joke/meme using movie footage as the
vehicle → this category).
spec.Deterministic tie-break rule:
**Rule I**: does the caption body itself
(not just account/hashtags) contain Tamil script, genuine Tanglish, or a
named Tamil-comedy cultural reference? → Tamil Comedy & Memes. Is the
Tamil signal confined to the account name or a single generic hashtag? →
Comedy & Entertainment (General).
spec.Language handling:
this is the category most directly defined by
language/cultural content — the whole point of Rule I is ensuring it
triggers on genuine content, not superficial labeling.
spec.Minimum evidence requirement:
genuine Tamil-script/Tanglish caption
text or a specific named cultural reference — explicitly *not* an account
name or single hashtag alone.
spec.General fallback interaction:
the confirmed weak spot in this
project's own prior classifier build — meme-format content is inherently
caption-light (the joke lives in the video), and an over-eager
thin-caption→General rule was found to systematically misroute genuine
Tamil Comedy content (0% precision/recall in one measured build). **This
category must not be penalized for having a short caption** if the
available text (even a few words) contains genuine Tamil/Tanglish/
cultural-comedy signal — length alone is not disqualifying here the way
it might be for a more text-dependent category.
spec.Review trigger:
content with a Tamil-sounding account but ambiguous
caption-body content — flag rather than defaulting either direction.

coconut-water-website case: `DdEmuLrpVtF`). Also excluded: content

genuine mindset/growth language with no specific

named relationship/person as the anchor (→ Relationships & Friendship).

exclusion rule), Relationships & Friendship (Rule B), Kollywood (the
unresolved `CrpNvDKvTTv` case, documented under Kollywood above).

**Rule B**: is the content anchored to
a *specific* relationship/person? → Relationships & Friendship. Is it

despite carrying motivational-sounding tags, because a specific
relational anchor is present.

subject, with a specific, well-evidenced

genuine mindset/growth content with no
overriding product or relationship anchor.

uncommon — motivational content tends
to carry recognizable, if generic, language.

any case where marketing/product language and
mindset language are both present and the "which is the actual subject"
call is close — flag (the `DdEmuLrpVtF` case was itself only correctly
resolved via a specific anti-magnetism rule, and even then landed
correctly only some of the time across different classifier attempts in
this project — this category has a genuinely confirmed history of being
mis-triggered, so err toward review over confident assignment when
